final_message:
All five functions are implemented in `problems.py`, stdlib-only, with signatures and docstrings untouched. Only `problems.py` is modified.

How each meets its spec:

- **`parse_duration`** (`problems.py:13`) — one anchored regex `(?:([0-9]+)h)?(?:([0-9]+)m)?(?:([0-9]+)s)?` via `fullmatch`. That single pattern enforces h→m→s ordering, rejects duplicates/out-of-order (`"30m1h"`, `"1h2h"` both fail to consume the whole string), bare units, whitespace, negatives, and trailing garbage. Non-string input raises `ValueError` via an explicit `isinstance` check; the empty string is rejected by the "at least one component" guard. `[0-9]` is used rather than `\d` so non-ASCII digits don't slip through.
- **`luhn_valid`** (`problems.py:38`) — strips spaces/hyphens, then scans right-to-left doubling every second digit with the `>9 → −9` fold. Never raises: non-string input, empty-after-strip, or any non-ASCII-digit character returns `False`.
- **`flatten`** (`problems.py:67`) — iterative explicit stack (safe against `RecursionError` on deep nesting — verified at 10,000 levels), joins with `sep`, drops empty nested dicts naturally, keeps lists (even dict-containing ones) as-is, and never mutates the input.
- **`top_k_frequent`** (`problems.py:92`) — counts with a plain dict, sorts by `(-count, word)` for the alphabetical tie-break, slices to `k`; `k <= 0` short-circuits to `[]`.
- **`rolling_max`** (`problems.py:107`) — monotonic deque of indices with descending values; each element is pushed and popped at most once, so it's O(n). Verified against brute force on 300 random inputs, and 400k elements with window 50k runs in 0.15s.

I also ran docstring examples verbatim plus edge cases (empty/`None`/bytes input, `"0h0m0s"`, mixed separators, case-sensitive ties, `window == len(nums)`, all-decreasing/all-tied windows) in a throwaway script, which passed and has been deleted. One test-script assertion of mine was initially wrong (miscounted nesting depth in the deep-flatten check); fixing the check, not the code, made everything pass.
